title: A presheaf formula for closed inverse image
statement:
For an affine closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ and a pro-etale
$\Lambda$-module sheaf $F$, with $\Lambda$ finite, $i^*F$ is the
sheafification on $\mathcal B_Z$ of
$$
 P_F(V)=F(v(V)).
$$
The formula includes sheafification; it does not presume the presheaf is
already a sheaf.

proof.text: Work directly in the category D of left Λ-modules, in the canonical fixed-scalar presentation already used in the Lean statement. Let RX and RZ be restriction from the full pro-etale sites to their affine bases. These restriction functors are equivalences for D-valued sheaves: shrink the existing limits in ModuleCat to the mixed size required by the affine basis comparison. Set v = closedSiteLift and r = closedSiteBaseChange. Obtain v ⊣ r from the closed-site adjunction and cocontinuity of v from the affine closed-site properties, hence continuity of r.

The opposite site adjunction, whiskered with D, gives precomposition by v.op left adjoint to precomposition by r.op on presheaves. Compose this adjunction with module-valued sheafification and restrict through the fully faithful inclusion of sheaves on the source. The result is L ⊣ R, where L(H) is the sheafification of v.op composed with H, and R is direct image along r. Mathlib Adjunction.op, Adjunction.whiskerLeft, Adjunction.comp and Adjunction.restrictFullyFaithful perform the natural Hom formulas and their triangle identities in the original plan, using actual linear maps throughout.

Base change commutes with inclusion of the affine bases into the full sites: r followed by toProEt Z is definitionally the same functor as toProEt X followed by full-site base change. The composition and natural-isomorphism comparisons for continuous sheaf pushforwards therefore give beta: i_* followed by RX is naturally isomorphic to RZ followed by R. Here i^* ⊣ i_* is the existing ModuleCat-valued upperStarLowerStarAdjunction.

Take the inverse mate of beta across i^* ⊣ i_* and L ⊣ R. Since RX and RZ are equivalences, the inverse-mate equivalence theorem makes this mate invertible. Its inverse is an isomorphism from i^* followed by RZ to RX followed by L. Evaluate it on the inverse realization of F. The latter composite is definitionally the module sheafification of (closedSiteLift followed by toProEt X).op composed with the underlying presheaf of that inverse realization. This is exactly the required isomorphism. Because all functors and adjunctions have values in ModuleCat Λ, every component and its inverse is already Λ-linear, with no commutativity assumption or additional transport of algebraic operations.
